about.title: Personal Injury Help in Indio, California
about.longDescription: Indio is home to roughly 87,500 people, and its streets stay busy all year. In 2025, the most recent year with final figures, the city recorded 201 injury collisions. Those crashes left 266 people injured and took 5 lives. Public collision records show the heaviest counts along Monroe Street, Indio Boulevard, Jackson Street, and Route 111, with reports tending to peak on Tuesdays between 2 p.m. and 4 p.m. These are simply the corridors Indio residents rely on every day. If a wreck, a fall, or a dog bite somewhere in the Coachella Valley has left you hurting, you may be juggling medical bills, missed shifts, and calls from an insurance adjuster all at once. We're here to help you focus on recovery. Tell us what happened, and we'll review your case. Our team handles personal injury claims in Riverside County. We work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. California allows two years to file most injury claims, and claims involving a government entity can carry a window as short as six months, so reaching out early keeps your options open.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Indio Claim

items.title: Two years to file, less against the government
items.desc: Most California injury claims must be filed within two years of the injury. If a city, county, or state agency is involved, the deadline can shrink to six months, so timing matters.

items.title: Partial fault does not shut the door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault. If you share some blame for what happened, your recovery is reduced by your percentage, not eliminated.

items.title: No cap on pain and suffering in ordinary cases
items.desc: For a typical injury claim in California, there is no statutory ceiling on non-economic damages like pain, distress, or lost enjoyment of life.

items.title: Contingency means no upfront cost
items.desc: We work on contingency. You pay no attorney fee unless there is a recovery in your case.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in California?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims, California allows two years from the date of injury. If your claim involves a government entity, such as a crash with a city vehicle or a fall on public property, the deadline may be as short as six months. Because those windows differ, it helps to get your situation reviewed promptly.

items.question: Are you a law firm?
items.answer: We handle personal injury claims directly. We do not give legal advice before you contact us; once you reach out, our team will review your case and discuss next steps with you.

items.question: What if the crash was partly my fault?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault. That means your compensation is reduced in proportion to your share of responsibility, but you are not barred from recovering. We can help sort out how fault is likely to be assigned in your situation.

items.question: How do we get paid?
items.answer: We work on a contingency basis. There is no fee unless there is a recovery, and the initial review costs you nothing. Fee details are agreed before any work begins.
